To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a low energy beta beam can be used to probe the existence of sterile neutrinos, and that (ii) a disappearance measurement is sufficient to constrain sterile neutrino properties without the need for a CP violation measurement, and that (iii) this can be done with moderate detector size and ion production rates.

a low energy, high intensity beta-beam facility can constrain the mixing angle of sterile neutrinos with the active neutrinos with high precision, and that a moderate detector size is sufficient to achieve this.
the low energy β-beam can be used to constrain mixing angles of sterile neutrinos as low as sin22θ≃10−2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of neutrino properties.
the study of the physics of neutrinos.
the study of the neutrino mass hierarchy and the search for new physics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a low energy β‐beam is the most promising facility to search for sterile states, provided that the detector is optimized for the detection of anti‐neutrino interactions.
a beta‐beam with a low energy electron neutrino beam could be used to probe the existence of sterile neutrino states.
a low energy β‐beam can provide a very competitive measurement of sterile neutrino oscillation parameters, with a sensitivity to sin22θ∼10−2 and Δm2∼1 eV2, and with a negligible background.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a low energy β‐beam can be a powerful tool to search for sterile states in the eV scale, with the advantage that it is free of hadronic uncertainties and can be used independently of the CP violating effects.

a low energy β-beam is a powerful facility to search for neutrino oscillations, and that the sensitivity is competitive with the one of a high energy β-beam, even though the former is less expensive and more flexible.

we have shown that a low energy β‐beam facility can constrain the sterile neutrino parameters at the same level as the current reactor and gallium experiments, but with much less background and systematic uncertainties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a low energy β‐beam is an excellent tool for the search of sterile neutrinos, which can be implemented with existing technology.
a low energy β‐beam is a very competitive facility for the discovery of sterile neutrinos.
the beta‐beam concept is not only a powerful tool to search for neutrino oscillations, but it can also be used to search in other domains.
